messages:
nate: Quick question — when we fall back from Hosted -> Private (customer VPC) during capacity pressure, what should the credential propagation model be? do we hand a long-lived API key to private control plane, or something ephemeral?

emma: Short answer: ephemeral. We should avoid leaking host-level keys to customer-owned infra.

lei: +1 ephemeral. But what shape? signed delegation token vs mTLS client cert? both have tradeoffs.

sam: mTLS is solid for mutual auth but messy for customer onboarding and cert rotation. signed tokens (JWT-like) are easier for one-off delegations.

nate: Agreed. Concern is: hosted control plane needs to be able to route a request to private runtime and let that runtime fetch model artifacts / kv-caches. We also need auditability and least privilege.

emma: Proposal: short-lived delegation JWT issued by Redwood KMS with audience=private-runtime and scope limited to {model:get, cache:read, inference:invoke}. TTL 5m. Private runtime presents it when fetching artifacts.

lei: That works for outbound calls from private runtime to our artifact store. For callbacks (runtime -> control plane) we need mutual auth for telemetry and logs. Use mTLS with server-auth only from runtime to CP and rotate via short-lived certs issued by our CA.

sam: To reduce customer friction, we can run a light client-side agent that handles cert renewals and token refresh. config sample: 
```
delegation:
  type: jwt
  ttl: 300s
  scopes: ["model:get","cache:read","inference:invoke"]
  issuer: redwood-kms
mtls:
  enabled: true
  ca: redwood-ca
  rotation: 1h
```

tammy: Important: customer private control plane should never see the root KMS material. Only signed tokens and certs. And we must emit audit events on issuance and revocation.

nate: Tradeoffs: signed tokens are replayable until expiry — mitigate with single-use nonce + artifact-bound audience claim. Also, we need to handle network partitions: if hosted can't reach private to rotate, runtime must fail-open or fail-closed?

emma: For security, fail-closed for artifact fetches (can't fetch model -> deny inference) but fail-open for telemetry (buffer and ship when back). We should document this explicitly.

lei: Ops concern: expiration storms — when many tokens expire simultaneously. Suggest staggered refresh windows and jitter in agent renewals.

sam: Also add graceful fallback: if private runtime cannot validate a delegation (clock skew), accept within a 60s leeway and emit a warning.

nate: Sounds like consensus. Action items:
1) Security to draft token schema (aud, scope, nonce, artifact-hash) and KMS signing API.
2) Infra to prototype agent that handles certs + token refresh with jitter.
3) Docs: clearly state fail-closed vs fail-open semantics and onboarding steps.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created issue RW-ops/2042 for token-schema and RW-ops/2043 for agent prototype :rocket:

tammy: I'll own the audit/event contract. Will add retention and sample events.

nate: Thanks — if anyone has objections to token TTL=5m+single-use-nonce approach, shout now. Otherwise we'll move forward with the above pattern. :thumbsup:

emma: No objections here.

lei: Fine by me.

sam: Looks good. I'll start the agent stub.

nate: Great. We'll schedule a short follow-up RFC to lock the exact token fields.
